To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the perspective display that best supports navigation performance is the one that best matches the perspective of the user.
the integration of others' perspectives and the incorporation of different views can improve users' performance on collaborative navigation tasks.

1) the integration of multiple perspectives in CVEs can enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of collaboration; 2) the use of a single perspective display can be effective for collaboration in some circumstances; 3) the use of multiple perspectives in a single display is not always better; and 4) the use of different perspectives for collaboration can be effective in certain circumstances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people collaborate in CVE, how they perceive and understand the virtual environment, and how to design better CVE interfaces to support collaborative activities.
how to design effective and efficient interfaces for collaborative navigation in a 3D environment, and how to evaluate them.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed perspective integration method is effective in supporting collaborative navigation in CVEs.
the integration of multiple perspectives into one display can help users to better understand others' perspectives and improve collaborative navigation.

the study of multiple perspective in collaborative navigation is still in the beginning stage, and more empirical studies are needed to explore the effectiveness of different multiple perspective displays on different collaborative tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 2.5D perspective display that combines both 3D perspective and 2D map views provides the best performance for collaborative navigation in a 3D virtual environment.
a 3D perspective display can help users to better understand the environment in a collaborative navigation task.
a single perspective display is not sufficient for supporting collaboration in 3D environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single perspective interface can be designed to integrate others' perspectives in a way that supports collaborative navigation.
a single perspective display can effectively integrate multiple perspectives and improve collaborative navigation performance.
integrating multiple views of others into a single user's view can be beneficial for collaborative navigation, but only if the views are integrated in a meaningful and coherent manner.
